summary: Fixed the GraphRun.started_at tie-break bug noted (not fixed) in FINAL_REPORT.md.
root_cause: Postgres now()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP returns the same value for every statement inside one transaction (unlike clock_timestamp()). Two GraphRun rows inserted in the same session_scope() got identical started_at, so ORDER BY started_at DESC could not reliably pick the later one.
fix: Added graph_runs.seq (BIGSERIAL, additive migration 20261013_0014), server_default=nextval('graph_runs_seq_seq') so the ORM omits it from INSERT and lets Postgres assign a distinct monotonically-increasing value per row regardless of transaction timing. Both 'latest run' queries in routers/graph.py now ORDER BY seq DESC instead of started_at DESC.

verification.regression_check: tests/test_graph_router.py + test_graph_sync_cli_db.py + test_graph_sync_state_db.py + test_graph_hub_flags.py: 33 passed. Full apps/api unit suite: 474 passed, no regressions.
verification.dev_live_check: docker compose exec api alembic upgrade head (20261013_0013 -> 20261013_0014) + api restart + GET /v1/graph/status returns 200 with the expected shape against dev's real DB

note: A caveat SQLAlchemy quirk was hit and fixed during this work: without an explicit server_default= hint on the mapped_column, SQLAlchemy's insertmanyvalues batching sends an explicit NULL for the column instead of omitting it, which violates the NOT NULL constraint even though the DB column itself has a working DEFAULT (BIGSERIAL's nextval). Fixed by adding server_default=text("nextval('graph_runs_seq_seq')") to the ORM mapping, mirroring the real DB default exactly.
